results.text: Dacia sales declined by 9.7% due to a transition in its product and powertrain cycle in the context of a strong acceleration of customer demand for EVs.
Q3, Renault Group sales declined by 6.0%, reflecting contrasting brand and regional dynamics.
In the meantime, Alpine maintained a strong growth momentum, with sales up 58.4%.
Commercial results highlights Over the first nine months of 2026 , Group sales totalled 1,662,222 vehicles, slightly down 2.2% compared with the same period in 2025.
Internationally, sales increased in the Group’s strategic markets, including India (+36.7%), T ürkiye (+3.2%), Morocco (+6.9%) and Brazil (+3.8%).
In the third quarter of 2026, against a backdrop of fierce competition, Renault Group sales totalled 497,799 vehicles, down 6.0%.

outlook.text: Total inventories remained at a healthy level (532,000 vehicles at September 30, 2026), while the European orderbook represented c.2 months of forward sales..

highlights: Over the first nine months of 2026 , Group sales totalled 1,662,222 vehicles, slightly down 2.2% compared with the same period in 2025. This headline reflects contrasted brand and regional dynamics.

In the third quarter of 2026, against a backdrop of fierce competition, Renault Group sales totalled 497,799 vehicles, down 6.0%. Yet in Europe the Group further improved the quality of its sales, with almost two out of every three passenger cars sold to retail customers over the period.

In Türkiye, Group sales declined by 18.0%, outperforming a market down 23.3%. In Latin America, the Group faced intense competition, with additional pressure in Argentina while the local market faced a 19.2% decline.

results.text: Recurring revenue accounted for 91.6% (87.1%) of total revenue. · Operating Result: SEK 15.4 million (SEK 5.6 million), an increase of 175%, driven by the 19% recovery in series production and lower operating expenses.

Recurring revenue accounted for 93.6% (92.9%) of the revenue. · Operating Result: SEK 29.1 million (SEK 27.0 million), an increase of 8%, supported by higher recurring revenue and lower operating expenses, despite prior-year net operating exchange gains of SEK 3.5 million.
Total revenue increased by 46% year-on-year to SEK 34.3 million, supported by higher series production volumes and higher Sampling Cup shipments.
Recurring revenue increased by 53% year-on-year to SEK 31.4 million, representing more than 91% of total revenue and marking the fourth consecutive quarter of recurring revenue growth.

The operating margin increased to approximately 45%, compared to 24% last year, demonstrating the strong financial leverage of our business model and our ability to translate higher production volumes into improved profitability.

outlook.text: The installation pipeline remains strong, with opportunities for new installations towards year-end, supporting our expectation that average annual installation revenues during 2026–2027 could exceed the historical level of approximately SEK 8 million.

highlights: · Revenue for Period: SEK 34.3 million (SEK 23.5 million), an increase of 45.6% year-on-year, primarily driven by the 19% recovery in series production, an 80% increase in Sampling Cup shipments. Recurring revenue accounted for 91.6% (87.1%) of total revenue.

· Operating Result: SEK 15.4 million (SEK 5.6 million), an increase of 175%, driven by the 19% recovery in series production and lower operating expenses. The operating margin improved to 44.8% (23.8%) demonstrating strong operating leverage.
· Earnings per Share: SEK 1.74 per share (SEK 0.62 per share).

results.text: Q3 2026 adjusted and reported sales increased by 4% at CER, driven by continued GLP-1 volume growth across the US and International operations, primarily in obesity.

results.text: Despite higher fixed costs, EBIT for the first nine months of the year amounted to DKK 977m, compared with DKK 785m in the corresponding period last year.
Profit & loss Revenue increased by 19% to DKK 5,807m in Q3 2026 from DKK 4,898m in Q3 2025, driven by higher volumes and increasing raw material prices, particularly marine fish oil and fish meal.

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 increased by 7% to DKK 13,172m from DKK 12,270m year to date in Q3 2025, primarily reflecting higher volumes, raw material prices and product and customer mix.
Other costs and other operating income and expenses increased year on year in Q3 2026 from DKK 352m to DKK 432m.
For the first nine months of 2026, other costs and other operating income and expenses increased year on year from DKK 929m to DKK 1,121m, reflecting the same matters as above.

outlook.text: Supported by the volume outlook, higher raw material prices and current exchange rates, BioMar raises its 2026 revenue guidance to DKK 17.8-18.6 billion range from previously DKK 17.0-18.0 billion.

results.text: Domestic’s third quarter 2026 underlying revenue totaled EUR 1,183 million, up +0.3% year-on-year on a pro forma basis, i.e. excluding the divestiture impact of Be-Mobile (including this impact, the revenue was down -0.7% year-on-year).

Wholesale Services revenue was up by +0.6%, including higher roaming revenue, continued growth in MVNO -revenue and increasing fiber wholesale volumes, nearly fully offset by the consolidation-effect of services delivered to Unifiber.

outlook.text: In this context, we raise our full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance for Proximus Global to EUR 125-135 million.

highlights: Domestic’s third quarter 2026 underlying revenue totaled EUR 1,183 million, up +0.3% year-on-year on a pro forma basis, i.e. excluding the divestiture impact of Be-Mobile (including this impact, the revenue was down -0.7% year-on-year).

Digia's Financial Calendar and Annual General Meeting in 2027
Inside information, profit warning: Digia lowers its 2026 guidance for EBITA operating profit

report.title: Digia Plc's Business review January-September 2026 (unaudited)

results.text: Our Q3 net sales were nearly on a par with last year’s level at EUR 49.0 (49.3) million and were entirely organic.
Operating profit (EBITA) was EUR 5.2 (5.2) million and the EBITA margin was 10.6 (10.5) percent, which was this year’s best quarterly result measured by profitability.
The service and maintenance business accounted for 53.4 (51.9) percent of net sales, up 2.3 percent.
Operating profit (EBITA) was EUR 11.6 (12.8) million and the EBITA margin was 7.2 (8.2) percent of net sales.
Operating profit was impacted by EUR 2 million in non-recurring expenses, of which EUR 1.1 million was linked to the write-down of customer projects and EUR 0.9 million to restructuring.

outlook.text: Profit guidance for 2026 New profit guidance for 2026, published on September 22, 2026: Digia’s profit guidance for 2026: Digia’s net sales will grow (EUR 217.0 million in 2025), and its operating profit (EBITA) (EUR 21.3 million in 2025) will fall compared to 2025.

Earlier profit guidance for 2026, published on February 5, 2026: Digia’s net sales will grow (EUR 217.0 million in 2025) and its operating profit (EBITA) (EUR 21.3 million in 2025) will either remain on a par with or increase compared to 2025.

highlights: Net sales EUR 49.0 (49.3) million, down 0.6%
Operating profit (EBITA) EUR 5.2 (5.2) million, up 0.5%; EBITA margin 10.6% (10.5%) of net sales
Operating profit (EBIT) EUR 4.6 (4.3) million, up 5.1%; EBIT margin 9.3% (8.8%) of net sales
sections.outlook: Digia’s profit guidance for 2026: Digia’s net sales will grow (EUR 217.0 million in 2025), and its operating profit (EBITA) (EUR 21.3 million in 2025) will fall compared to 2025.

outlook.text: Outlook for 2026 (last updated on June 10, 2026) REVENUE Kemira's revenue is expected to be between EUR 2,600 and EUR 3,000 million in 2026 (2025 revenue: EUR 2,753.5 million).

We reiterate our financial outlook for the year and expect our 2026 revenue to be between EUR 2,600 million and EUR 3,000 million and our 2026 operative EBITDA to be between EUR 400 million and EUR 500 million.

Financial targets Kemira has the following long-term financial targets to support its growth strategy; Kemira’s target is to achieve an annual organic growth rate of over 4%, to maintain an operative EBITDA margin within the range of 18–21% and to maintain operative ROCE above 16%.

highlights: • Revenue increased by 3%, amounting to EUR 708.9 million (687.7), mainly driven by acquisitions. Revenue in local currencies, excluding acquisitions and divestmen ts, was stable.

sections.outlook: The demand in Kemira's end-markets remains weak due to continued global economic uncertainty and geopolitical tensions and the raw material and logistics cost environment continues to be volatile. outlook.text: The order backlog was boosted to a record EUR 3.4 billion by a landmark IPTO framework agreement..

highlights: a-EBITDA amounted to EUR 446 million, up 18% (H1 2025: EUR 378 million), supported by improved performance across nearly all segments.
